prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: production grass foliage cutout atlas for a realistic 3D game, square 2048x2048 RGBA with genuine transparent background.
Composition: FOUR separate narrow upright grass bunches side by side in FOUR equal-width vertical columns across one square image. All root bases aligned close to the bottom edge (94% of image height), and tips reaching between 8% and 20% from the top. Each bunch fits entirely inside its own quarter of the image, with clear transparent margins; no overlap between columns. Frontal orthographic view of individual modest grass bunches, each 16–24 slim grass leaves rising from a small dark root group. Most leaves upright with relaxed natural curvature, a few gently drooping sideways; unequal heights and delicate irregular tips. No needle spikes, no wide cartoon ribbons, no flowers, no wheat seed heads.
Subject/material: photogrammetry-grade real rough meadow grass, realistic green and yellow-olive blades with dark moss-green roots, olive-green middle sections, subtly lighter khaki green tips. Individual leaves have smooth natural colour gradients along their length and delicate midribs, some warm spent leaves among the fresh green. Four different natural silhouettes with slight colour variation, muted realistic palette, fine detailed grass but soft subdued contrast.
Lighting: de-lit texture appearance under broad diffuse overcast light, gentle interior root occlusion, no strong directional lighting or harsh highlights.
Constraints: genuinely transparent pixels behind and BETWEEN every leaf; no ground patch, no soil mound, no pot, no cast shadow, no rectangle background, no grey checkerboard, no text, no grid lines, no border. This is an atlas of photographed grass plant cutouts, not a picture of a field.
usage: Four independent botanical bunch cutouts on distant grass LODs beyond 40 metres. Shader alpha cutoff 0.5, with muted olive chroma and no tree-crown mip footprint growth. Foreground grass uses individual folded blades with procedural colour gradients; sparse real-blade shadow meshes preserve contact without casting every photographed leaf.
